Hi Elena / Rohan — following up with the technical evidence bundle. High level answers first, full links below.

1) Residency options: Redwood supports three routing patterns:
   - EU-only execution: inference and short-term KV cache pinned to EU regions (recommended when customer requires strict locality).
   - Contractual routing + audit: requests routed to nearest region by default, but controller can specify EU-only routing via account policy (logs and attestations provided).
   - Private on-prem option for air-gapped deployments.

2) KV/cache: We do not persist full request bodies in long-term storage. KV cache is ephemeral (configured TTL default 15 minutes) and can be disabled; we can include sanitized config showing no disk-backed persistence for EU-flagged keys.

3) KMS & key rotation:
   - We integrate with customer-managed KMS (recommended) or Redwood-managed KMS.
   - Key rotation cadence: default 90 days; we publish rotation events to SIEM.

4) Subprocessors: Attached is the current roster with region and data access level. Short list: GCP (europe-west1) — infra; S3-compatible object store (eu-central) — logs; VectorOps (model optimization partner, us-east) — only receives model weights (no customer plaintext unless explicitly enabled).

Links & attachments:
- redwood-dpf-evidence-summary.pdf [Attachment stub]
- TIA-Novara-annotated.xlsx (completed template attached)
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNovara-TIA (contains diagrams, SIEM schema, anonymized SOC extract)

Marissa added a short DPA annex redline (see attached in the Drive). Ben — SOC extract included as sanitized page 2-3 per our disclosure policy.

If helpful, I can do a 30-minute technical walkthrough with your security team tomorrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
